title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 135
paragraphs: Not only is the courage shown by these men worthy of admiration, but also the sayings they uttered. On their way to Susa they came to Hydarnes — a Persian by birth, commander of the peoples of the Asian seaboard — and he offered them hospitality and entertained them. While they were his guests he asked them: “Lacedaemonians, why do you refuse to become friends of the king? You can see that the king knows how to honor good men, if you look at me and my fortunes. So you too, Lacedaemonians, if you gave yourselves over to the king — since you already have the reputation with him of being good men — each of you would rule some Greek country as the king's gift.” To this they answered: “Hydarnes, your advice to us is not equally balanced, for you advise having experience of one side only and no experience of the other. You know well what slavery is, but you have never yet tasted freedom, to know whether it is sweet or not. If you had tried it, you would advise us to fight for it not with spears only, but with axes.”
